metadata.scope: Two additive, backward-compatible parser relaxations: R1 = `;`-separated statement sequences in `=` function bodies (kills PAR017); R2 = newline-as-soft-separator inside `{ }` blocks (kills PAR020). R1 ships first; R2 merges ONLY after the corpus AST-diff fuzz pass is green. NON-SCOPE: `ailang fmt` formatter (deferred to m-ailang-fmt.md follow-up stub — D1); significant indentation; match...with; tuple-type `;` slip; the rig A/B (deferred to mission controller as a post-merge measurement, NOT an in-sprint gate).
metadata.verification_binary: read-only against HEAD v0.29.2 (std/VERSION); parser sources read live, NOT rebuilt (plan is doc + JSON only, no code touched)
metadata.fmt_discrepancy_resolution: Option (b): `ailang fmt` DOES NOT EXIST (no fmt case in cmd/ailang/main.go dispatch, no formatter package). Deferred to its own follow-up doc design_docs/planned/v0_29_0/m-ailang-fmt.md. In-sprint canonical form = golden parse fixtures (same AST) + doc/prompt guidance. The v1.0 bar names 'm-syntax-ai-forgiving landed' = parser accepts the forms; it does NOT require fmt.
metadata.phasing_gate: R1 (M1) -> R1 fuzz gate (M2, zero re-parse diffs) -> R2 (M3) -> R2 fuzz gate + full suites (M4, zero re-parse diffs). If the R2 fuzz gate goes red, R1 still merges independently and R2 is reworked/deferred (report R1-only outcome + apply D8 dialect-card wording rule).
metadata.in_sprint_acceptance: parser fixtures (all Conflict-Surface fixtures) + corpus AST-diff fuzz zero-diff (benchmarks/**/*.ail + examples/**/*.ail, currently-valid files) + make verify-examples baseline + full Go suites (make test) + make lint + make check-file-sizes.
metadata.deferred_gpu_step: The rig A/B on local models (old vs new parser, `;`-family benchmarks, 5 trials, 1M-token cap, compile_error delta) is the REAL success metric but is a GPU step. It is DEFERRED to the mission controller as a post-merge measurement under rig_lock_acquire wait — NOT an in-sprint acceptance gate. Current eval rotation is cloud-only (holds no rig lock).
metadata.magnitude_caveat: The ~32% figure is from the June qwen3-5 corpus and predates the v0.29.0 frontier-tier re-grade — the failure CLASS is live-proven at HEAD (PAR017/PAR020 still fire on the near-miss forms), its current share is unmeasured. Treat the number as directional; the deferred A/B is the real metric.

discrepancies_found.action: Fuzz corpus glob = benchmarks/**/*.ail AND examples/**/*.ail; assert identical ASTs only for files the OLD parser currently accepts with zero errors.

discrepancies_found.finding: The `=` body branch (parser_func.go:182-198) calls parseExpression(LOWEST) ONCE then wraps in ast.Block. It does NOT call parseFunctionBody (that is the `{ }` branch at parser_func.go:207). R1 needs its OWN `;`-sequence loop in the `=` branch.
discrepancies_found.action: R1 adds a statement-sequence loop directly in the `=` branch (with peekIsDeclBoundary()); do not route the `=` body through parseFunctionBody.

discrepancies_found.finding: peekStartsBlockStatement (parser_expr.go:476) checks ONLY token type (LET/LETREC/IF/MATCH/IDENT) — no line awareness. The line comparison must be added at the call sites as p.peekToken.Line > p.curToken.Line. Precedent: parser_expr.go:53 already does exactly this comparison for the GAP2 LPAREN fix.
discrepancies_found.action: R2 continue-condition = peekTokenIs(SEMICOLON) OR (peekStartsBlockStatement() AND p.peekToken.Line > p.curToken.Line) at both block loops.

discrepancies_found.finding: There are TWO independent block `;`-loops: parseFunctionBody (parser_func.go:343, for func...{} bodies) AND parseBlockOrExpression (parser_expr.go:424, for standalone {} block expressions incl. if/else branch blocks). Both currently loop only `for p.peekTokenIs(SEMICOLON)`. A single-site fix leaves one block form (e.g. if...then {newline-block}) still emitting PAR020.
discrepancies_found.action: Systemic fix: R2 must patch BOTH loops identically. The `if...then {newline-block}` fixture forces both to be patched.

discrepancies_found.finding: missingBlockSemicolonError() PAR020 guard fires in TWO places: parser_func.go:212 (after parseFunctionBody) and parser_expr.go:443 (after parseBlockOrExpression).
discrepancies_found.action: R2's 'keep PAR020 for same-line no-`;`' must preserve BOTH guards; each fires only when the line-check is false (same line) after the newline rule is added.

discrepancies_found.finding: Trap #2 = the `;`-in-`=`-body rule (R1 target). Trap #3 = match-arm commas (a Conflict-Surface item, unaffected). If R2 is deferred behind the fuzz gate and only R1 lands, deleting trap #2 would drop still-live newline-in-block guidance.
discrepancies_found.action: If R1+R2 BOTH land -> reword/remove trap #2 (both rules relaxed). If ONLY R1 lands -> REWORD trap #2 to keep the newline-in-block guidance; do NOT delete. Trap #3 untouched.

features.description: R1: accept `;`-separated statement sequences in `=` function bodies. In parseFunctionDeclaration's `=` branch (parser_func.go:182-198), replace the single parseExpression(LOWEST) with a loop parsing `expr (; expr)*` that stops at a declaration boundary, wrapping the exprs in the existing ast.Block. Add peekIsDeclBoundary() = export|type|import|EOF OR (func followed by IDENT). `func (` (anonymous-function expression) is NOT a boundary and stays in the body (D4 — own loop, not parseFunctionBody).

risks: R1 `func IDENT` vs `func (` lookahead insufficient (M-TAINT v0.14.3 precedent: a 2-token lookahead passed hand-picked tests but mis-parsed ~14 real programs). Mitigation: funclit-in-=-body fixture (M1) + corpus fuzz (M2) before R1 merges.

R2 patched at only ONE of the two block loops (D6) — leaves if/then-branch blocks still emitting PAR020. Mitigation: the if...then {newline-block} fixture forces both parseBlockOrExpression and parseFunctionBody to be patched.

R2 newline rule misfires on a multi-line expression. Mitigation: continue only when peekStartsBlockStatement() (type) AND peek.Line > cur.Line; operators excluded so line-split expressions never split.
Record literal mis-read as two statements. Mitigation: up-front record/record-update detection (parser_expr.go:407/414) stays ahead of the loop; explicit record fixtures in M3.
Canonical-form erosion (two accepted forms, no `ailang fmt`). Mitigation (accepted): golden parse fixtures (same AST) + documented canonical form + tracked m-ailang-fmt.md follow-up (D1 option b).
CHANGELOG targeting: do NOT edit changelogs/v0.10-current.md (does not exist as current) — use changelogs/v0.18-current.md (D2).
The rig A/B is the real metric but MUST NOT be treated as an in-sprint gate — it is a GPU step deferred to the mission controller under rig_lock_acquire wait.
